Definition: Older adult action lets caregivers reserve attention for unresolved events.
Sub-theme: Reminders support routines when familiar cues recede
Theme: The agent supports routines while people retain care
Example quote: I only check when there is something to check. (C04, Phase 2, L29)
Reflexivity note: Self report does not establish independent action in every event.

Definition: Relatives connect medicine with meals, location, work, and bodily circumstances absent from a schedule.
Sub-theme: Reminders support routines when familiar cues recede
Theme: The agent supports routines while people retain care
Example quote: Phone does not know if I have eaten or if I am outside. (P04, Phase 2, L93)
Reflexivity note: The agent cannot replace contextual knowledge held by people.

Definition: Portable prompts matter when travel, fieldwork, gatherings, or changed routines remove familiar cues.
Sub-theme: Reminders support routines when familiar cues recede
Theme: The agent supports routines while people retain care
Example quote: At home my wife can tell me. In the field there is nobody asking. (P06, Phase 2, L179)
Reflexivity note: This is reported usefulness, not an adherence outcome.

Definition: Repeated reminders can make dose times easier to anticipate without replacing existing routines.
Sub-theme: Reminders support routines when familiar cues recede
Theme: The agent supports routines while people retain care
Example quote: Maybe it has reinforced the timing. (P11, Phase 2, L110)
Reflexivity note: The leading interview prompt prevents a cognitive improvement claim.

Definition: People remain responsible for correct medicine, interpretation, supply, and repair.
Sub-theme: Reminders support routines when familiar cues recede
Theme: The agent supports routines while people retain care
Example quote: Less pressure, not less responsibility. (C04, Phase 2, L33)
Reflexivity note: Caregiver relief does not transfer accountability to the agent.

Code: The agent takes clock watching work
Definition: Scheduled reminders reduce the need for caregivers to remember every dose time.
Sub-theme: Reminders support routines when familiar cues recede
Theme: The agent supports routines while people retain care
Example quote: I don't have to remember every medicine time myself. (C03, Phase 2, L33)
Reflexivity note: Reported relief is not an objective workload measure.

Definition: Proposed photo capture supports setup only when a person checks the extracted medication instruction.
Sub-theme: Simple interaction distributes care work without taking over
Theme: The agent supports routines while people retain care
Example quote: If there is doubt, we ask the doctor or pharmacy. (P04, Phase 2, L221)
Reflexivity note: Prescription capture was not implemented.

Definition: Relatives may configure schedules while older adults recognize, confirm, question, and take medicine.
Sub-theme: Simple interaction distributes care work without taking over
Theme: The agent supports routines while people retain care
Example quote: My daughter set it up for me. After that, the reminder part was easy. (P05, Phase 2, L7)
Reflexivity note: Setup help is not treated as nonuse.

Definition: Clear timing, Bangla speech, large text, medicine images, and few controls support direct response.
Sub-theme: Simple interaction distributes care work without taking over
Theme: The agent supports routines while people retain care
Example quote: Simple one. Big writing, medicine picture, voice reminder, one button to say taken. [...] That's enough. (P04, Phase 2, L257)
Reflexivity note: Medicine images and selectable reminder modes were not deployed.

Definition: Stable setup and selective alerts let the agent remove more coordination work than it creates.
Sub-theme: Simple interaction distributes care work without taking over
Theme: The agent supports routines while people retain care
Example quote: it should help us, not make another job for us. (C04, Phase 2, L233)
Reflexivity note: Maintainability conditions continued delegation.

Definition: Proposed low supply notices reach the family member who can obtain medicine.
Sub-theme: Simple interaction distributes care work without taking over
Theme: The agent supports routines while people retain care
Example quote: A reminder before it runs out would help. (C06, Phase 2, L187)
Reflexivity note: Stock sensing was not deployed.

Definition: Configuration or supply help does not necessarily transfer the medication action.
Sub-theme: Simple interaction distributes care work without taking over
Theme: The agent supports routines while people retain care
Example quote: I don't need someone to put it in my hand. I can take it myself. (P08, Phase 2, L185)
Reflexivity note: This protects task specific agency.

Definition: The first prompt reaches the older adult or caregiver already responsible for the next action.
Sub-theme: Existing care roles determine the first prompt
Theme: Older adults control when the agent involves family
Example quote: Mostly it reminded me, because I am the one managing their medicines. (C05, Phase 2, L17)
Reflexivity note: Caregiver led dosing prevents a universal older adult first rule.

Definition: An audible statement makes the agent's current service relationship understandable.
Sub-theme: Existing care roles determine the first prompt
Theme: Older adults control when the agent involves family
Example quote: When it said it is working for me, I understood it better. (P10, Phase 2, L13)
Reflexivity note: The spoken Bangla service announcement was deployed.

Definition: Family access becomes unacceptable when it expands beyond medication information.
Sub-theme: Permission and limits keep handoffs reversible
Theme: Older adults control when the agent involves family
Example quote: If it shared private family information that was not about the medicine, that would not be okay. (C05, Phase 2, L177)
Reflexivity note: This hypothetical boundary limits the agent's mandate.

Definition: An unresolved event goes to one chosen caregiver rather than the whole family.
Sub-theme: Permission and limits keep handoffs reversible
Theme: Older adults control when the agent involves family
Example quote: One family member is enough. (P13, Phase 2, L130)
Reflexivity note: The missing household map prevents recipient specific claims.

Definition: Routine success and small delays do not justify wider family disclosure.
Sub-theme: Permission and limits keep handoffs reversible
Theme: Older adults control when the agent involves family
Example quote: normal medicine reminders should remain with me. (P17, Phase 2, L126)
Reflexivity note: This refusal prevents collective care from becoming compulsory disclosure.

Definition: The agent asks before involving family, and older adults may decline or stop the handoff.
Sub-theme: Permission and limits keep handoffs reversible
Theme: Older adults control when the agent involves family
Example quote: Then I stopped the family alert because there was no need to worry them. (P10, Phase 2, L31)
Reflexivity note: Merged request and refusal because together they define a changeable handoff; no logs show its frequency.

Definition: Another reminder and waiting period should come before contacting family.
Sub-theme: Permission and limits keep handoffs reversible
Theme: Older adults control when the agent involves family
Example quote: First remind them again after some time. (C02, Phase 2, L40)
Reflexivity note: Risk graded escalation was not implemented.

Definition: A warning needs the medicine, event, and reason for contacting another person.
Sub-theme: Nonconfirmation prompts a question rather than a verdict
Theme: Caregivers act on uncertain exceptions, not automatic judgments
Example quote: it should also tell me why it is giving the warning (C07, Phase 2, L36)
Reflexivity note: This evaluates a described escalation, not deployed risk reasoning.

Definition: Medicine may be taken without a phone confirmation, while confirmation cannot prove ingestion.
Sub-theme: Nonconfirmation prompts a question rather than a verdict
Theme: Caregivers act on uncertain exceptions, not automatic judgments
Example quote: I had actually taken it, I just forgot the phone part. (P05, Phase 2, L19)
Reflexivity note: Older adult and caregiver accounts both identify this record gap.

Definition: Incorrect missed dose claims create unnecessary family concern and weaken attention to later alerts.
Sub-theme: Nonconfirmation prompts a question rather than a verdict
Theme: Caregivers act on uncertain exceptions, not automatic judgments
Example quote: everyone would start worrying unnecessarily. (C06, Phase 2, L55)
Reflexivity note: No logs establish an alert accuracy rate.

Definition: No confirmation should prompt a question rather than a missed dose claim.
Sub-theme: Nonconfirmation prompts a question rather than a verdict
Theme: Caregivers act on uncertain exceptions, not automatic judgments
Example quote: the family should check instead of assuming. (P14, Phase 2, L57)
Reflexivity note: Both roles preserve human interpretation of the event.

Definition: Work, conversation, travel, delay, or an unheard prompt can produce no response.
Sub-theme: Nonconfirmation prompts a question rather than a verdict
Theme: Caregivers act on uncertain exceptions, not automatic judgments
Example quote: Silence does not necessarily mean I have forgotten. Sometimes I am simply busy. (P11, Phase 2, L48)
Reflexivity note: Patterned interpretation of silence was not deployed.

Definition: Doctors or pharmacists clarify changes while the agent represents an existing routine.
Sub-theme: People verify the agent before relying on it
Theme: Caregivers act on uncertain exceptions, not automatic judgments
Example quote: For medicine changes, doctor and family should discuss. (P10, Phase 2, L65)
Reflexivity note: The agent remains a tool rather than a prescriber.

Code: Error or maintenance burden revokes use
Definition: Wrong content, excessive alerts, hidden changes, or repeated upkeep can end reliance.
Sub-theme: People verify the agent before relying on it
Theme: Caregivers act on uncertain exceptions, not automatic judgments
Example quote: if it becomes too much work to maintain, then we probably won't use it. (C04, Phase 2, L193)
Reflexivity note: This prospective condition shows when delegation ends.

Definition: Older adults and caregivers verify names and times before reducing routine checking.
Sub-theme: People verify the agent before relying on it
Theme: Caregivers act on uncertain exceptions, not automatic judgments
Example quote: For some days I still kept the old written information nearby. (C04, Phase 2, L149)
Reflexivity note: This was lived checking, not the unimplemented probationary mode.

Code: Prescription and medicine strip anchor truth
Definition: People compare agent information with prescriptions, packages, notes, and established routines.
Sub-theme: People verify the agent before relying on it
Theme: Caregivers act on uncertain exceptions, not automatic judgments
Example quote: The prescription is the authority for me. (P15, Phase 2, L43)
Reflexivity note: Both roles place material records above agent output.

Definition: Agreement with known schedules allows less checking of stable reminders.
Sub-theme: People verify the agent before relying on it
Theme: Caregivers act on uncertain exceptions, not automatic judgments
Example quote: I don't need to check every time. But for a new medicine I still check. (C03, Phase 2, L153)
Reflexivity note: Trust remains limited to a verified routine.

Definition: Streak loss can upset an older adult, while family response redirects attention to the next dose.
Sub-theme: Medicine remains separate from game performance
Theme: Streaks show care work, while medicine remains primary
Example quote: my son said, okay, it happened, take the next one properly. (P10, Phase 2, L79)
Reflexivity note: Merged grief and repair because the family response shows how metric harm is contained.

Definition: Medicine taking continues for routine and clinical reasons rather than to maintain progress.
Sub-theme: Medicine remains separate from game performance
Theme: Streaks show care work, while medicine remains primary
Example quote: The medicine is the main thing. Score is just extra. (C03, Phase 2, L129)
Reflexivity note: Older adult and caregiver accounts converge on this boundary.

Definition: Competition, constant checking, blame, or anxiety makes progress feedback unacceptable.
Sub-theme: Medicine remains separate from game performance
Theme: Streaks show care work, while medicine remains primary
Example quote: If it becomes another performance measure, then no. (P11, Phase 2, L92)
Reflexivity note: This constrains the coach role.

Definition: A streak lets involved relatives notice sustained medication work without turning it into public performance.
Sub-theme: Progress makes routine care work visible
Theme: Streaks show care work, while medicine remains primary
Example quote: It became something they could see. But they don't need to make a big thing about it. (P07, Phase 2, L107)
Reflexivity note: Older adult approval is limited to modest family recognition.

Definition: A streak can make represented medication work visible to older adults and caregivers within the family.
Sub-theme: Progress makes routine care work visible
Theme: Streaks show care work, while medicine remains primary
Example quote: It was showing that the medicines were being given regularly. (C06, Phase 2, L99)
Reflexivity note: Merged display and comment codes because both concern recognition, not motivation.

Definition: Conversational health sharing does not permit automatic sharing of medication records or scores.
Sub-theme: Community experience prompts questions, not medicine changes
Theme: Friends and community support care, while doctors guide medicine
Example quote: Family can see, other people don't need to. (P04, Phase 2, L137)
Reflexivity note: Collective care still requires chosen access boundaries.

Definition: Conflicting medicine stories can burden older adults rather than support care.
Sub-theme: Community experience prompts questions, not medicine changes
Theme: Friends and community support care, while doctors guide medicine
Example quote: I listen, but I don't want the phone adding more confusion. (P07, Phase 2, L195)
Reflexivity note: Community connection is not assumed beneficial.

Definition: Other people's medicine experiences can lead to consultation without authorizing treatment changes.
Sub-theme: Community experience prompts questions, not medicine changes
Theme: Friends and community support care, while doctors guide medicine
Example quote: If many people are saying something, I may ask the doctor about it. But asking is different from taking it. (P15, Phase 2, L191)
Reflexivity note: This is elicited reasoning, not observed consultation.

Definition: Use by known peers can make unfamiliar technology seem more trustworthy.
Sub-theme: Older adults give and receive care beyond family
Theme: Friends and community support care, while doctors guide medicine
Example quote: If other farmers use it and say it works, I will trust it more. (P06, Phase 2, L199)
Reflexivity note: Social trust does not establish technical accuracy.

Definition: Older adults remind and check other people as well as receive care.
Sub-theme: Older adults give and receive care beyond family
Theme: Friends and community support care, while doctors guide medicine
Example quote: I also ask her about her medicine. So it is both ways. (P06, Phase 2, L79)
Reflexivity note: Older adults are not positioned only as care recipients.

Definition: Hearing another person discuss medicine can draw attention back to one's own routine.
Sub-theme: Older adults give and receive care beyond family
Theme: Friends and community support care, while doctors guide medicine
Example quote: If someone says they have to take their tablet, sometimes I remember mine. (P04, Phase 2, L241)
Reflexivity note: Community discussion was elicited from a subset.
